content: The current diabetes management standards established by the American Diabetes Association (ADA) emphasize that achieving lower A1C levels in children under the age of six may increase the risk of hypoglycemia. Therefore, it is critical to individualize treatment plans for this population to balance glycemic control with safety. In certain situations, maintaining higher A1C levels may be advantageous. For example, during the honeymoon phase of diabetes, when some residual endogenous insulin production is still present, preserving this function can facilitate glycemic management and reduce the burden of strict glucose control.
